title: SWIFT-linked fraudulent transfers at a commercial bank
summary: Reuters reported that attackers compromised the SWIFT system of a Kathmandu commercial bank during the festival holidays and moved about USD 4.4 million to accounts in several countries. The central bank said most of the money was recovered, with about USD 580,000 outstanding.
notes: Described as Nepal's first reported cyber heist. Date is the Reuters report date; the theft happened the month before. NPR value is an approximate conversion of USD 4.4 million.

title: DDoS attack disrupts government data-centre services
summary: A Kathmandu Post column reported that immigration and passport management databases hosted at the Government Integrated Data Centre were disrupted by a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack.
notes: Date is the publication date of an opinion column, so the incident itself may be slightly earlier.

title: DDoS attacks take hundreds of government websites offline
summary: The National Information Technology Centre said hundreds of government websites went offline on 31 December and 1 January because of DDoS attacks on the government's main data centre.
notes: The Cabinet later decided to set up a National Cyber Security Centre on 23 January 2024.

title: NPR 34.2 million taken from a payments company's corporate bank account
summary: Naya Patrika reported that attackers accessed the online banking of a fintech company's corporate account at a commercial bank and made unauthorised transfers worth about NPR 34.2 million. Police opened an investigation after a formal complaint.
notes: Police said the investigation was at a preliminary stage. No attribution is made here.

title: Aviation authority and airport websites defaced
summary: Nepali ICT reported that the aviation regulator's website and several airport websites were defaced with political messages. The authority showed a maintenance notice and said its data remained secure.
notes: Claims made by any group are deliberately not recorded. Airport locations are shown at city level only.

organisation: Department of National ID and Civil Registration
title: National ID department website defaced
summary: ICT Frame reported that the department's public information website was compromised and taken offline as a precaution. A Home Ministry spokesperson said the main National ID database was not affected.
notes: The affected site was reported to hold general information rather than National ID records.

title: Government email addresses found in public breach data
summary: After Nepal joined a global breach-notification service, officials found at least 135 official government email addresses exposed in data breaches, including accounts at several ministries. The National Cyber Security Centre said affected departments were being notified and passwords reset.
notes: Exposure was identified through breach monitoring; the dates of the original breaches are not stated.

title: Phishing emails impersonating government and police offices
summary: The National Cyber Security Centre said it detected phishing emails sent in the names of the Prime Minister's Office and senior police officers, with threats of prosecution meant to panic recipients into sharing personal data.

title: Commercial-bank login records reported circulating online
summary: A TechPana investigation reported over 9,000 login records linked to staff, administrators and customers of commercial banks circulating online. It attributed them mainly to password reuse and infostealer exposure rather than a breach of core banking systems.
notes: No bank has been shown to have suffered a breach of core systems. Individual banks are deliberately not listed.

title: Ransomware at a brokers' data centre halts stock trading
summary: A ransomware attack on a data centre hosting the trading systems of 72 brokerage firms disrupted trading systems, CDSC-related systems and payment gateways. NEPSE suspended trading on 21 September at the brokers' request while affected systems were isolated and assessed.
notes: Brokers placed the attack at about 4am on 20 September. The extent of any data impact was still being assessed when reported.

title: Government websites taken offline over a critical PHP flaw
summary: After a critical vulnerability was disclosed in widely used PHP software, the Software Development and Operation Center said several government websites and portals were temporarily taken offline as a precaution. Services are being restored gradually after patching.
notes: Precautionary shutdown; the notice cites potential rather than confirmed compromise. The Kathmandu Post reports that some banks also took websites offline.
